This file provides the code and analysis for Harrison et al (2026) *“Acoustic enrichment and mass larval release amplify coral settlement success”* as referenced in the main text and methods.

## Methods

### Spatial interpolation and visualization of tile-scale settlement patterns

To visualize fine-scale spatial heterogeneity in coral settler densities, individual settlement tile data were first projected to a common planar coordinate system (`EPSG:20353`). Coordinates were recentred per site × treatment group by subtracting each group’s centroid and rounding to 0.1 m.

Settlement intensity was mapped as a continuous surface by spatial interpolation of point observations (tile locations) within each treatment and within each site × treatment combination. Point‐based settlement values were treated as samples from an underlying spatial field, and predictions were generated on a regular grid spanning the experimental footprint.

Interpolation used inverse distance weighting (IDW), which estimates the value at each grid cell as a weighted mean of nearby observations, with weights declining as a power function of distance; this provides a smooth surface that reflects local structure while avoiding strong distributional assumptions. Inverse distance weighting (IDW) interpolation was applied to log-transformed settler counts using the gstat package with an inverse-distance power of 4.5 to emphasize local spatial structure while minimizing the influence of distant points. To reduce artefacts from extrapolating beyond the sampled area, predicted surfaces were clipped to a buffered convex‐hull footprint defined by the set of tile locations within each group, so contours are shown only where sampling support exists.

For treatment-level summaries, gridded predictions were aggregated across sites at each grid cell to obtain a mean treatment surface. Spatial patterns were visualised as filled contour maps on an equal-distance coordinate system, and mean flow direction vectors were overlaid to aid interpretation of settlement gradients relative to prevailing hydrodynamic direction.

### Bayesian spatial modelling of coral settlement

To quantify treatment effects on coral settler abundance while accounting for spatial dependence and site-level variation, we fitted a Bayesian hierarchical spatial model using the brms package (Bürkner, 2017) with a negative binomial response distribution to accommodate overdispersed counts:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log \mu_i
&=
\beta_0
+
\beta_{\text{treatment}[i]}
+
\beta_{\text{flow}}\,\text{flowspeed}_i
+
\beta_{\mathrm{HC}}\,\text{hard\_coral}_i
+
\beta_{\mathrm{HC}}\,\text{surface\_area\_ratio}_i
+
f(x_i, y_i)
+
b_{\text{site}[i]} \\
b_{\text{site}[i]}
&\sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{\text{site}}^2) \\
\text{total\_settlers}_i
&\sim \text{NegBinomial}(\mu_i,\phi)
\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
Y_i \sim \mathrm{NegBin}(\mu_i, \phi)
$$

The response variable (`total_settlers`) was log-transformed nad modelled as a function of experimental treatment, mean flow speed over the 12hr period post-release at each site (`flowspeed`), local benthic cover as derived from images (`hard_coral`), and SAR (surface-area-ratio) derived from Digital Elevation Models (DEM) from orthomosaics at each site. All covariates and coordinates were centred and scaled.

Spatial autocorrelation was captured through a smooth bivariate term `s(x_lon, y_lat, k = n-1)` which models continuous spatial structure in longitude–latitude space across the 24 treatment plots using thin-plate regression splines (Wood 2021). This smooth term accounts for residual spatial variation among sites beyond the fixed effects. Random effects were specified as varying intercepts by site (1 \| site), reflecting the nested design in which each site received a single treatment. This structure allows observations within a site to share a common deviation from the overall treatment mean, accounting for site-level heterogeneity without implying correlation or shared treatment effects across sites. Because sites are unique to treatments, this formulation avoids over-parameterisation and ensures stable estimation of treatment differences given levels of replication.

Weakly regularising priors were specified to stabilise estimation while preserving interpretability: `Normal(0, 2)` for fixed effects, and `Exponential(1)` for random effect standard deviations `(sd)`, spline standard deviation `(sds)`, and the negative-binomial shape parameter `(shape)`. The model was fitted with four MCMC chains, each with 4000 iterations (2000 warmup), using the NUTS sampler with adapt_delta = 0.999 and max_treedepth = 15 to ensure stable convergence (Rhat \< 1.01 for all parameters).

Posterior predictions were generated for each treatment under mean covariate conditions (population-level, no random effects). Expected settler counts and treatment contrasts (ratios) were summarised with median and 95% credible intervals, and visualized using half-eye plots and ridge-density plots to highlight effect magnitudes and uncertainty.

Smooth-term and hyperparameter posteriors were extracted to assess spatial variability and overdispersion. The spline standard deviation (`sds(sx_lony_lat_1)`) quantifies the overall amplitude of spatial variation, while the shape parameter characterizes the degree of overdispersion relative to a Poisson process.

All analyses were conducted in R (v4.3) using `brms`, `tidybayes`, and `ggplot2`.

```{r}
tilecounts <- readxl::read_xlsx(here("data", "LarvalAcousticTileData_LIRS2024_NewPositionChanges.xlsx")) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(position = tile_plot_position_code_1_14) |>
  rename(plot_id = new_plot_id) |>
  dplyr::select(site, position, plot_treatment, plot_id, tile_tag_id, total_settlers) |>
  mutate(site = substr(plot_id, 1, 2)) |>
  mutate(treatment = substr(plot_id, 3, 10)) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels=c("C", "A", "L", "LA"))) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = recode(
      treatment,
      "C"  = "control",
      "A" = "acoustic",
      "L" = "larval",
      "LA" = "larvalacoustic"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(site = str_replace(site, "^S", "S")) |>
  dplyr::select(-plot_treatment, -plot_id) |>
  mutate(total_settlers = as.numeric(total_settlers)) |>
  mutate(log_settlers = log10(total_settlers)) |>
  mutate(log_settlers = ifelse(is.infinite(log_settlers), 0, log_settlers))

                rubble_loose_84, rubble_consolidated, dead_hard_coral_structure_86, sand_87, other) |>
  rename(rubble_loose=rubble_loose_84, turf_algae=turf_algae_83, dead_hard_coral_structure=dead_hard_coral_structure_86, sand=sand_87) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(survey_title_2, treatment_3, site_4), names_to="category", values_to="cover") |>
  rename(site=site_4) |>
  mutate(treatment = substr(survey_title_2, 3, 10)) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = recode(
      treatment,
      "C"  = "control",
      "A" = "acoustic",
      "L" = "larval",
      "LA" = "larvalacoustic"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-survey_title_2, -treatment_3) |>
  group_by(site, treatment, category) |>
  summarise(cover=mean(cover)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = category,
    values_from = cover,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |> mutate(site=paste0("S", site))

times <- data.frame(
  site=c("B6", "B5", "B5", "B6", "B4", "B4", "B3", "B3", "B2", "B2", "B1", "B1"),
  treatment = c("L", "LA", "L", "LA", "L", "LA", "LA", "L","LA", "L","LA", "L"),
  time = c("15:40", "16:05", "16:20", "16:30", "16:46", "16:57", "17:24", "17:40", "17:52", "18:05", "18:20", "18:30")
) |>
  mutate(
    datetime = as.POSIXct(paste("2024-11-26", time),
                          format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",
                          tz = "Australia/Brisbane")
  )

# min time per site
sites_min <- times |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(min_time = min(datetime), .groups = "drop")

# add new rows for "A" and "CA" at each site's min time
new_rows <- tidyr::crossing(sites_min, treatment = c("A", "C")) |>
  transmute(site, treatment, datetime = min_time)

# combine and order
release_times <- bind_rows(times, new_rows) |>
  arrange(site, datetime) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("C", "A", "L", "LA"))) |>
  dplyr::select(-time)


# ensure POSIXct
release_times <- release_times %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime, tz = "Australia/Brisbane"))

flow <- flow %>%
  mutate(date = as.POSIXct(date, tz = "Australia/Brisbane"))

# crop each site × treatment to 12 h after its release time
flow_12h <- flow %>%
  inner_join(release_times, by = c("site", "treatment")) %>%
  filter(date >= datetime, date <= datetime + hours(12)) %>%
  arrange(site, treatment, date)

flow_12h_release <- flow_12h |>
  group_by(site, treatment) |>
  filter(date == datetime) |>
# summarise(date=date, speed = first(speed), bearing=first(bearing),.groups = "drop") |> 
  summarise(date=date, speed = mean(speed), bearing=mean(bearing),.groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(treatment = recode(treatment,
                            L = "larval",
                            A = "acoustic",
                            LA = "larvalacoustic",
                            C = "control")) |>
  mutate(site = stringr::str_replace(site, "^B(\\d+)$", "S\\1"))# |> 
#  select(-date)



flow_utm <- left_join(site_coords,flow_12h_release) |> 
  st_transform(32755)

k   <- 4
p   <- 2
eps <- 1e-9

known_all <- which(is.finite(flow_utm$speed) & is.finite(flow_utm$bearing))
miss      <- which(!is.finite(flow_utm$speed) | !is.finite(flow_utm$bearing))

if (length(miss) > 0) {
  flow_utm[miss, c("speed", "bearing")] <- purrr::map_dfr(miss, function(i) {
    tr <- flow_utm$treatment[i]
    
    known_t <- known_all[flow_utm$treatment[known_all] == tr]
    known   <- if (length(known_t) >= 2) known_t else known_all
    
    d <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(flow_utm[i, ], flow_utm[known, ]))
    ord <- order(d)
    ord <- ord[seq_len(min(k, length(ord)))]
    
    nn  <- known[ord]
    dd  <- d[ord]
    
    w <- 1 / ((dd^p) + eps)
    w[dd < eps] <- 1e12
    
    sp <- flow_utm$speed[nn]
    br <- flow_utm$bearing[nn]
    
    sp_hat <- sum(w * sp) / sum(w)
    
    th <- br * pi / 180
    br_hat <- atan2(sum(w * sin(th)), sum(w * cos(th))) * 180 / pi
    if (br_hat < 0) br_hat <- br_hat + 360
    
    tibble(speed = sp_hat, bearing = br_hat)
  }) %>% as.data.frame()
}

flow_df <- flow_utm |> as.data.frame() |> select(-geometry)
```

### Spatial footprints of acoustic and larval restoration

Across treatments, interpolated settlement surfaces show clear spatial structure in larval-addition treatments but little to no structure in controls. The control panel is uniformly low across the footprint, indicating minimal settlement throughout the plot. Acoustic enrichment alone shows patchy, weakly elevated areas but remains dominated by low values. In contrast, larval addition produces a distinct settlement “hotspot” near the centre of the plot, with values declining outward, consistent with localized accumulation of settlers. The combined larval + acoustic treatment shows the strongest and most concentrated hotspot, suggesting the highest settlement intensity and the steepest spatial gradient away from the peak, while remaining low across most of the surrounding area.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 12


# ---- packages ----
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(gstat)
library(ggplot2)


global_idp <- 3
global_nmax <- 6
global_res <- 0.25
global_buffer <- 1.2

treat_levels <- c("control", "acoustic", "larval", "larvalacoustic")

standardise_treatment <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(as.character(x))
  x <- gsub("[^a-z]", "", x)
  x <- dplyr::recode(x,
                     "larvallacoustic"  = "larvalacoustic",
                     "larvalacoustic"   = "larvalacoustic",
                     "control"          = "control",
                     "acoustic"         = "acoustic",
                     "larval"           = "larval"
  )
  factor(x, levels = treat_levels)
}

mask_to_group <- function(r, df_group, buffer_km = global_buffer) {
  geom <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_geometry(df_group))
  hull <- sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(geom))
  buf  <- sf::st_buffer(hull, dist = buffer_km)
  v    <- terra::vect(buf)
  terra::crs(v) <- ""
  terra::crop(r, v, mask = TRUE)
}

idw_raster <- function(df_pts,
                       value_col = "log_settlers",
                       ext_m = 2.75,
                       res_m = global_res,
                       idp = global_idp,
                       nmax = global_nmax,
                       maxdist_km = NA_real_) {
  
  stopifnot(inherits(df_pts, "sf"))
  stopifnot(value_col %in% names(df_pts))
  
  df_pts <- df_pts %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(.data[[value_col]]))
  
  if (nrow(df_pts) < 3) return(NULL)
  
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(df_pts)
  pts <- df_pts %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]) %>%
    sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = NA)
  
  grid_df <- expand.grid(
    x = seq(-ext_m, ext_m, by = res_m),
    y = seq(-ext_m, ext_m, by = res_m)
  )
  grid_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(grid_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = NA)
  
  fml <- stats::as.formula(paste0(value_col, " ~ 1"))
  
  idw_sf <- gstat::idw(
    formula = fml,
    locations = pts,
    newdata = grid_sf,
    idp = idp,
    nmax = nmax,
    maxdist = if (is.na(maxdist_km)) Inf else maxdist_km
  )
  
  pred_df <- cbind(grid_df, pred = idw_sf$var1.pred)
  
  r <- terra::rast(pred_df, type = "xyz", crs = "")
  names(r) <- "settlers.pred"
  r
}



# ---- (A) pooled-by-treatment rasters
main_groups <- counts_sf %>%
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) %>%
  dplyr::group_split()

main_names <- counts_sf %>%
  dplyr::distinct(treatment) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(treatment) %>%
  dplyr::pull(treatment) %>%
  as.character()

main_idw_all <- setNames(
  lapply(main_groups, function(df) {
    r <- idw_raster(df, value_col = "log_settlers")
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    mask_to_group(r, df, buffer_km = global_buffer)
  }),
  main_names
)

# polygons for pooled-by-treatment (for outlines)
main_poly_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(main_groups, function(df) {
  geom <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_geometry(df))
  hull <- sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(geom))
  buf  <- sf::st_buffer(hull, dist = 1)
  p <- buf %>%
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
    sf::st_coordinates() %>%
    as.data.frame()
  p$treatment <- standardise_treatment(df$treatment[1])
  p
}))

df_main <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(main_idw_all), function(nm) {
  r <- main_idw_all[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::rename(value = settlers.pred) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(nm, levels = treat_levels))
})) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(value, breaks = seq(0, 1.6, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE))

# ---- (B) site × treatment rasters 
# priority: site×treat (this group) -> pooled treat (all sites) -> pooled global
global_r <- {
  r <- idw_raster(counts_sf, value_col = "log_settlers")
  if (!is.null(r)) mask_to_group(r, counts_sf, buffer_km = 1) else NULL
}

pair_groups <- counts_sf %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site, treatment) %>%
  dplyr::group_split()

pair_names <- counts_sf %>%
  dplyr::distinct(site, treatment) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(id = paste(site, as.character(treatment), sep = "_")) %>%
  dplyr::pull(id)

pair_idw_all <- setNames(lapply(pair_groups, function(df) {
  # try within-group
  r1 <- idw_raster(df, value_col = "log_settlers")
  
  # fallback to pooled treatment
  tr <- as.character(df$treatment[1])
  r2 <- main_idw_all[[tr]]
  
  # fallback to global
  r_use <- if (!is.null(r1)) r1 else if (!is.null(r2)) r2 else global_r
  
  if (is.null(r_use)) return(NULL)
  mask_to_group(r_use, df, buffer_km = global_buffer)
}), pair_names)


brks <- seq(0, 3, 0.2)


df_pairwise <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(pair_idw_all), function(nm) {
  r <- pair_idw_all[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  site <- stringr::str_extract(nm, "^S\\d+")
  tr   <- stringr::str_extract(nm, "(control|acoustic|larval|larvalacoustic)$")
  as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::rename(value = settlers.pred) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      site = site,
      treatment = factor(tr, levels = treat_levels)
    )
})) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(value, breaks = seq(0, 1.6, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    bin_id  = as.integer(cut(value, breaks = brks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)),
    binlow  = dplyr::if_else(is.na(bin_id), NA_real_, brks[bin_id]),
    binhigh = dplyr::if_else(is.na(bin_id), NA_real_, brks[bin_id + 1L]),
    binmean = (binlow + binhigh) / 2
  )
 
# polygons for site×treatment outlines
group_poly_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(pair_groups, function(df) {
  geom <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_geometry(df))
  hull <- sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(geom))
  buf  <- sf::st_buffer(hull, dist = 1)
  p <- buf %>%
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
    sf::st_coordinates() %>%
    as.data.frame()
  p$site <- df$site[1]
  p$treatment <- df$treatment[1]
  p
}))
```

### Impacts of acoustic and larval restoration

**(a)** Settler counts (log scale) increase across treatments, with lowest values in **Control**, intermediate in **Larvae** and **Acoustic**, and highest (and most variable) in **Larvae + Acoustic**; points/lines show site-level responses and consistently shift upward with treatment intensity. **(b)** Posterior distributions for treatment contrasts (multiplicative scale) show strong evidence that **acoustic/control (\~×3.5)**, **larval/control (\~×61.7)**, and **larval+acoustic/control (\~×87.3)** exceed 1 (Pr(\>1)=1.00), while **larval+acoustic/larval (\~×1.4)** is weaker (Pr(\>1)=0.83). **(c)** The distribution of the “increment” (log10 axis) places most mass well above 1, with the highlighted distributions indicating a higher median increment for the combined treatment (blue; median ≈ 49.6) relative to the comparator (red; median ≈ 35.4).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)



fit_base <- readRDS("/Users/rof011/acoustics/data/fit_base.rds")

# ---- population-level newdata (match fit_base covariates) ----
cov_means <- counts_df %>%
  summarise(
    speed     = mean(speed,    na.rm = TRUE),
    hard_coral  = mean(hard_coral, na.rm = TRUE),
    sar = mean(sar, na.rm=TRUE),
    site_x        = mean(site_x,        na.rm = TRUE),
    site_y        = mean(site_y,        na.rm = TRUE)
  )

pop_nd <- tibble(
  treatment    = factor(c("control","acoustic","larval","larvalacoustic"),
                        levels = levels(counts_df$treatment)),
  speed    = cov_means$speed[1],
  hard_coral = cov_means$hard_coral[1],
  sar = cov_means$sar[1],
  site_x        = cov_means$site_x[1],
  site_y        = cov_means$site_y[1]
)

# ---- posterior expected counts per treatment (population-level; no REs) ----
epred_pop <- add_epred_draws(pop_nd, fit_base, re_formula = NA) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(.draw, treatment, .epred)

# ---- expected counts summary ----
pop_sum <- epred_pop %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  mean_qi(.epred, .width = 0.95) %>%
  ungroup()

# ---- contrasts (ratios) ------------------------------------------------------
contr_draws <- epred_pop %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = .epred) %>%
  transmute(
    .draw,
    `larvalacoustic / larval` = larvalacoustic / larval,
    `larvalacoustic / control` = larvalacoustic / control,
    `larval / control`        = larval / control,
    `acoustic / control`      = acoustic / control
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-.draw, names_to = "contrast", values_to = "ratio") %>%
  filter(is.finite(ratio), ratio > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    contrast = str_replace_all(contrast, " / ", "/"),
    contrast = factor(contrast,
                      levels = c("larvalacoustic/larval",
                                 "larvalacoustic/control",
                                 "larval/control",
                                 "acoustic/control"))
  )

contr_summary <- contr_draws %>%
  group_by(contrast) %>%
  summarise(
    median  = median(ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    low95   = quantile(ratio, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi95    = quantile(ratio, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    Pr_gt1  = mean(ratio > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    medianlabel = paste0("x", round(median, 1)),
    pr_label    = sprintf("Pr(>1)=%.2f", Pr_gt1)
  )


inla_dat_df_site <- counts_df |> group_by(treatment, site) |> summarise(settlers=mean(exp(log_settlers)))

# ---- raw-scale increment draws ----------------------------------------------
raw_inc_draws <- epred_pop %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = .epred) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    .draw,
    C  = control,
    L  = larval,
    A  = acoustic,
    LA = larvalacoustic,
    inc_L   = L  - C,
    inc_A   = A  - C,
    inc_LA  = LA - C,
    inc_add = inc_L + inc_A,               # additive expectation (raw scale)
    d_inc   = inc_LA - inc_add,            # difference (0 = raw-additive)
    OE_inc  = inc_LA / pmax(inc_add, 1e-9) # ratio (1 = raw-additive); guard small denom
  )

# ---- medians for label positions --------------------------------------------
median_df <- raw_inc_draws %>%
  dplyr::select(
    `observed increment (LA - C)`            = inc_LA,
    `additive increment ((L - C) + (A - C))` = inc_add
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to  = "contrast",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(value > 0) %>%   # keep only positive (log10 scale)
  dplyr::group_by(contrast) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    median  = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Extended Figures

### Extended Data Fig. 1 Sound

Power spectral density (PSD) curves reveal the effect of acoustic enrichment on sound levels within the experimental plots. (a) PSD for triaxial particle acceleration levels averaged across 2-min samples at each of 13 (of 14 available) tiles at one site with playback off and on, measured ?? cm above the seafloor. Window length = 2048 points, overlap = 50%, window = Hann. The playback signal elevated spectra above ambient levels at 50 and 100 Hz, and above 1000 Hz. (b) PSD for sound pressure levels from eight 5-minute samples taken from high tide and low tide across 4 days during the experiment at 10 sites for both ambient and playback treatments, measured at the seafloor, mean is given in bold. Window length = 48000 points, overlap = 50%, window = Hann; The playback signal elevated spectra above ambient levels below 300 Hz, and at various frequencies above 300 Hz, depending on the plot. (c) PSD for sound pressure levels averaged across 2-min samples at each of 13 tiles at one site with playback off and on, measured ?? cm above the seafloor. Window length = 2048 points, overlap = 50%, window = Hann. The playback signal elevated spectra above ambient levels below 400 Hz and above 1000 Hz.

### Extended Data Fig. 2 Posterior estimates from the negative binomial hierarchical model

Posterior effect estimates from the hierarchical negative binomial model (log link) fitted to settler counts (n = 333). Top panel shows fixed-effect coefficients on the log scale (points = posterior medians; thick/thin intervals = 50%/95% credible intervals) with the dashed vertical line at zero (no effect). Bottom panel shows key hyperparameters: the smooth term standard deviation for the spatial spline s(\mathrm{site\_x}, \mathrm{site\_y}) and the negative binomial shape parameter (dispersion).

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 6

library(posterior)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidybayes)
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(tidybayes)
library(posterior)
draws <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit_base)
nms   <- names(draws)

# ----------------------------
# Fixed effects (+ smooth basis)
# ----------------------------
fix_cols <- grep("^(b_|bs_)", nms, value = TRUE)

p_fixed <- draws %>%
  select(all_of(fix_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "term_raw", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    term = term_raw |>
      str_remove("^b_") |>
      str_remove("^bs_") |>
      str_replace("^sx_lony_lat_1$", "s(x_lon,y_lat)[1]") |>
      str_replace("^sx_lony_lat_2$", "s(x_lon,y_lat)[2]") |>
      str_replace("^speed$", "Flow speed") |>
      str_replace("^sar$", "Rugosity") |>
      str_replace("^hard_coral$", "Coral cover") |>
      str_replace("^treatmentacoustic$", "Acoustic") |>
      str_replace("^treatmentlarval$", "Larval") |>
      str_replace("^treatmentlarvalacoustic$", "Larval + Acoustic")
  ) %>%
  filter(!term_raw %in% c("bs_ssite_xsite_y_1", "bs_ssite_xsite_y_2")) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(fct_inorder(term)), x = value)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.2) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.90, .50), point_interval = "median_qi", linewidth=0.8, size=1.2,
               color = "skyblue4", fill = "skyblue2", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Coefficient (log link)", y = "") +
  theme_bw()

# ----------------------------
# Hyperparameters: include sds + shape
# ----------------------------
hyper_cols <- unique(c(grep("^sds_", nms, value = TRUE), "shape"))

p_opt <- draws %>%
  select(all_of(hyper_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "term_raw", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(
    term = term_raw |>
      str_replace("^sds_", "") |>
      str_replace("^sx_lony_lat_1$", "s(x_lon,y_lat)") |>
      str_replace("^sx_lony_lat_2$", "s(x_lon,y_lat)") |>
      str_replace("^ssite_xsite_y_1$", "s(x,y)") |>
      str_replace("^ssite_xsite_y_2$", "s(x,y)") |>
      str_replace("^shape$", "Shape") |>
      str_replace("^\\((.*)\\)$", "\\1") |>
      str_replace_all("_", " ")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(fct_inorder(term)), x = value)) +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.90, .50), point_interval = "median_qi", linewidth=0.8, size=1.2,
               color = "coral4", fill = "coral", linetype = 0.2, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Hyperparameters", y = "") +
  theme_bw()

fig_s1 <- (p_fixed / p_opt) + plot_layout(heights = c(0.85, 0.15))

fig_s1

ggsave(fig_s1, filename="/Users/rof011/acoustics/plots/fig_s1.pdf", width=10, height=4.5)

```

### Extended Data Fig. 3 Spatial patterns of settlement within plots

Across six sites (rows S1–S6) and four treatments (columns), the panels map the within-plot spatial distribution of settlement using interpolated surfaces, with warmer colours indicating higher predicted settler counts and cooler colours indicating low/zero settlement. Control plots are uniformly low with little spatial structure, whereas acoustic treatments show modest, patchy increases that vary among sites. Larval additions produce clear, localised hotspots (often near the plot interior rather than edges), and the combined larval+acoustic treatment generally shows the strongest and most spatially concentrated peaks, though hotspot position and intensity differ by site. Overlaid arrows indicate contemporaneous flow direction(s), providing context for whether high-settlement patches align with prevailing transport within each plot footprint (black outline), and highlighting that settlement responses are spatially heterogeneous and site-specific rather than uniformly elevated across the whole plot.

### Fig S1. Site distances

Distribution of nearest Site×Treatment distances. Kernel density estimate (filled curve) of the nearest-neighbour distance (m) between each tile and the closest tile belonging to a different site × treatment unit. Points along the x-axis show individual observations (rug), dashed vertical line marks the mean nearest-neighbour distance.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 9


library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

# pairwise distance matrix (m) across ALL rows (no site restriction)
D <- st_distance(site_coords) |> as.matrix()

n <- nrow(site_coords)
diag(D) <- Inf

nn_idx  <- apply(D, 1, which.min)
nn_dist <- D[cbind(seq_len(n), nn_idx)]

nn_tbl_sitecoords <- tibble(
  site              = site_coords$site,
  treatment         = as.character(site_coords$treatment),
  nearest_site      = site_coords$site[nn_idx],
  nearest_treatment = as.character(site_coords$treatment[nn_idx]),
  distance_m        = as.numeric(nn_dist)
)

mean_distance <- mean(nn_tbl_sitecoords$distance_m)

ggplot(nn_tbl_sitecoords, aes(x = distance_m)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 0.4, adjust = 1, alpha = 0.2, fill = "aquamarine3") +
  geom_point(aes(distance_m, 0), shape = 21, alpha = 0.2, fill = "transparent") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(nn_tbl_sitecoords$distance_m, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(
    x = "Nearest-neighbour distance (m)",
    y = "Density",
    title = "Nearest-neighbour distances from each site centroid (n = 24))"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

  dplyr::filter(grepl("acoustic", treatment))
```

### Fig S2. Site images

Ortho images

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false


library(tidyverse)
library(fs)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(gt)

# --- Use RELATIVE paths under the project root (Quarto preview won't serve absolute /Users/...) ---
files_abs <- dir_ls(here("images"), glob = "*.jpg")
files_rel <- path_rel(files_abs, start = here())  # e.g. "images/B1C_....jpg"

# sanity check
missing <- files_rel[!file_exists(path(here(), files_rel))]
if (length(missing)) message("Missing relative paths:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))

# parse site/treatment from filenames like "B3CA_*.jpg"
image_table <- tibble(file_rel = files_rel) |>
  mutate(base = basename(file_rel)) |>
  mutate(mat  = stringr::str_match(base, "^(B\\d+)([A-Z]+)")) |>
  transmute(
    site      = stringr::str_replace(mat[,2], "^B", "S"),
    treatment = mat[,3],
    file_rel
  ) |>
  arrange(site, treatment, file_rel) |>
  distinct(site, treatment, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("C","CA","LR","LRA"))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = site, names_from = treatment, values_from = file_rel) 

# ensure columns exist and order
for (nm in c("C","CA","LR","LRA")) if (!nm %in% names(image_table)) image_table[[nm]] <- NA_character_
image_table <- image_table |>
  dplyr::select(site, C, CA, LR, LRA) |>
  mutate(across(-site, ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "", paste0('<img src="', .x, '" width="300px">'))))

# --- Option A: kable (keeps relative paths; works with Quarto preview & embed-resources) ---
knitr::kable(
  image_table,
  format = "html",
  escape = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Site", "Control", "Acoustic", "Larval", "Larval + Acoustic")
) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r}
    site = as.factor(stringr::str_replace(site, "^B", "S")),

bar_df <- flow_bar %>%

bar_df <- bar_df %>%

missing_panels <- tibble(

)


ggplot() + theme_bw() +

  geom_text(data = missing_panels, aes(x = date, y = speed, label=label), color="darkred", alpha=0.6) +

  ) +
```

### Rugosity

Surface Area Ratio (SAR) by treatment and site. Bars show the mean SAR for each treatment (control, acoustic, larval, larval+acoustic) within each site (S1–S6). SAR is a dimensionless rugosity metric computed as the ratio of 3D surface area to the corresponding planar (2D) area for each plot/patch-reef tile; values \>1 indicate increasing surface complexity relative to a flat surface. For each site, SAR was calculated per unit (e.g., tile/plot) from the underlying orthomosaic derived Digital Elevation Model (DEM), then aggregated as the mean within treatment × site for plotting.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10


metrics <- c("mean","sd","min","max","range","iqr","vrm","sar")

rugosity_site_means <- rugosity %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    across(all_of(metrics), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_tiles = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(site)


rugosity %>%
  mutate(
    site = factor(site),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control","acoustic","larval","larvalacoustic"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(treatment = fct_recode(treatment, Control = "control", Acoustic = "acoustic", Larval = "larval", "Larval + Acoustic" = "larvalacoustic")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = sar, group = site)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = treatment), , colour="black", alpha = 0.7, show.legend=FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scales::brewer_pal(palette = "YlGnBu")(4)[1:4]) +
#  geom_line(aes(color = site), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 3) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "SAR")

```

### Benthic patterns

Benthic substrate composition by site and treatment. Rows show sites (S1–S6) and columns show treatments (Acoustic, Control, Larvae, Larvae & acoustic). Within each panel, horizontal bars give the percentage cover of each substrate component (Turf algae, Soft coral, Sand, Rubble loose, Rubble consolidated, Other, Hard coral, Dead hard coral structure). Across sites and treatments, turf algae is consistently the dominant cover category, and hard coral is generally a smaller fraction than turf algae with modest variance among sites. 

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 10
#| 


library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

benthic_long <- benthic %>%
  mutate(treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "control","acoustic","larval","larvalacoustic")) %>%
  mutate(treatment = fct_recode(treatment, 
                                "Control" = "control", 
                                "Acoustic" = "acoustic", 
                                "Larval" = "larval", 
                                "Larval + Acoustic" = "larvalacoustic")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(site, treatment),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "percent"
  ) %>%
  mutate(component = component %>% str_replace_all("_", " ") %>% str_to_title())

colorplot <- c("bisque4", "coral", "deeppink", "lightgoldenrod", "lightgoldenrod4", "tan", "turquoise1", "chartreuse4")
names(colorplot) <-   c("Dead Hard Coral Structure", "Hard Coral", "Other", "Rubble Consolidated", 
    "Rubble Loose", "Sand", "Soft Coral", "Turf Algae")
  
ggplot(benthic_long, aes(x = component, y = percent, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color="black") +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_grid(site ~ treatment) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colorplot) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

### Model output & posterior predictive check (grouped means)

Posterior summary for the hierarchical negative binomial model (log link) fitted to settler counts (n = 333). Reported are posterior means (Estimate), posterior SD (SE), 95% credible intervals (CI\_\text{low}–CI\_\text{high}), convergence diagnostics (Rhat, Bulk_ESS, Tail_ESS), and incidence rate ratios (IRR = exp(Estimate)) with 95% credible intervals for fixed effects. Spatial smooth basis coefficients and hyperparameters (site random-intercept SD, smooth SD, and negative binomial shape) are shown on the log/scale-parameter scales (IRR not applicable).

```{r}

library(brms)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

fit <- fit_base
s   <- summary(fit)

fmt_block <- function(x, section) {
  x %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    mutate(section = section) %>%
    select(section, term, Estimate, Est.Error, `l-95% CI`, `u-95% CI`, Rhat, Bulk_ESS, Tail_ESS) %>%
    rename(
      SE      = Est.Error,
      CI_low  = `l-95% CI`,
      CI_high = `u-95% CI`
    )
}

fixed_tbl <- fmt_block(s$fixed, "Fixed effects") %>%
  mutate(
    IRR     = exp(Estimate),
    IRR_low = exp(CI_low),
    IRR_hi  = exp(CI_high)
  )

sds_tbl <- if (!is.null(s$sds) && nrow(as.data.frame(s$sds)) > 0) {
  fmt_block(s$sds, "Smooth hyperparameters") %>%
    mutate(term = str_replace(term, "^sds\\((.*)\\)$", "sds(\\1)"))
} else {
  tibble()
}

rand_tbl <- if (!is.null(s$random) && "site" %in% names(s$random) && nrow(as.data.frame(s$random$site)) > 0) {
  fmt_block(s$random$site, "Random effects (site)") %>%
    mutate(term = str_replace(term, "^sd\\((.*)\\)$", "sd_site(\\1)"))
} else {
  tibble()
}

spec_tbl <- if (!is.null(s$spec_pars) && nrow(as.data.frame(s$spec_pars)) > 0) {
  fmt_block(s$spec_pars, "Distributional") %>%
    mutate(term = str_replace(term, "^shape$", "shape (negbin)"))
} else {
  tibble()
}

pub_tbl <- bind_rows(fixed_tbl, sds_tbl, rand_tbl, spec_tbl) %>%
  mutate(
    term = term %>%
      str_replace("^Intercept$", "(Intercept)") %>%
      str_replace("^treatment", "treatment: ") %>%
      str_replace("^ssite_xsite_y_([0-9]+)$", "s(site_x, site_y)[\\1]")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(Estimate, SE, CI_low, CI_high, Rhat), ~ round(.x, 2)),
    across(c(Bulk_ESS, Tail_ESS), ~ round(.x, 0)),
    across(c(IRR, IRR_low, IRR_hi), ~ round(.x, 2))
  )

caption_txt <- paste0(
  "Negative binomial model (log link). N = ", s$nobs,
  ". Formula: total_settlers ~ treatment + speed + hard_coral + sar + s(site_x, site_y, k = 23) + (1 | site)."
)

pub_tbl %>%
  mutate(
    IRR = if_else(section == "Fixed effects", as.character(IRR), NA_character_),
    IRR_low = if_else(section == "Fixed effects", as.character(IRR_low), NA_character_),
    IRR_hi = if_else(section == "Fixed effects", as.character(IRR_hi), NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = caption_txt,
    col.names = c("Block", "Term", "Estimate", "SE", "95% CI low", "95% CI high", "IRR", "IRR 95% low", "IRR 95% high", "Rhat", "Bulk ESS", "Tail ESS"),
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")) %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top") %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Posterior (log scale)" = 4, "IRR (fixed only)" = 3, "Diagnostics" = 3))

pri_tbl <- prior_summary(fit) %>%
  transmute(class, coef, group, dpar, nlpar, resp, prior)

shape_tbl <- summarise_draws(as_draws_df(fit) %>% select(shape)) %>%
  as_tibble() 

readr::write_csv(pub_tbl, here("data", "maintbl.csv"))
readr::write_csv(pri_tbl, here("data", "priortbl.csv"))
readr::write_csv(shape_tbl, here("data", "shptbl.csv"))

```

Observed group means (dark lines) lie well inside the posterior predictive distributions for all treatments. Control and acoustic show slight right-tail skew in $$T(y_{\text{rep}})$$, consistent with NB overdispersion; larval and larvalacoustic are well captured around \~30 and \~90–100 respectively.

### Spatial autocorrelation tests

Residuals including the spatial smooth and site random slopes show a small negative spatial autocorrelation: Moran’s I=-0.031 (null E\[I\]=-0.003), Z=-2.58. With the default greater alternative the p-value is 0.995, indicating no evidence of positive autocorrelation. Interpreted two-sided, the result implies a statistically detectable but tiny negative autocorrelation, suggesting the fitted spatial surface has absorbed most structure and any remaining SAC is negligible in magnitude.

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 10
#| 

library(tidybayes)
library(spdep)

# 1) Newdata aligned to the fitted model (includes site/treatment + scaled covariates)
df0 <- counts_df %>%
  dplyr::select(total_settlers, site, treatment, hard_coral, 
                speed, sar, site_x, site_y) %>% #, tile_x, tile_y) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(.row = row_number())

# 2) Posterior expected means (includes site REs & smooth)
ep_incRE <- add_epred_draws(df0, fit_base, re_formula = NULL)

res_mu_incRE <- ep_incRE %>%
  group_by(.row) %>%
  summarise(mu_hat = mean(.epred), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(df0, by = ".row") %>%
  mutate(resid = total_settlers - mu_hat)

# # compute residuals EXCLUDING REs (population-level field)
# ep_noRE <- add_epred_draws(df0, fit_sp1, re_formula = NA)
# 
# res_mu_noRE <- ep_noRE %>%
#   group_by(.row) %>%
#   summarise(mu_hat = mean(.epred), .groups = "drop") %>%
#   left_join(df0, by = ".row") %>%
#   mutate(resid = total_settlers - mu_hat)

# 3) Build a connected neighbour graph automatically (k-NN, symmetrised)
find_connected_knn <- function(coords, k_min = 8, k_max = 30) {
  for (k in k_min:k_max) {
    knn <- spdep::knearneigh(coords, k = k)
    nb  <- spdep::knn2nb(knn, sym = TRUE)
    if (spdep::n.comp.nb(nb)$nc == 1) return(list(nb = nb, k = k))
  }
  knn <- spdep::knearneigh(coords, k = k_max)
  nb  <- spdep::knn2nb(knn, sym = TRUE)
  list(nb = nb, k = k_max)
}

coords_mat <- as.matrix(df0[, c("site_x","site_y")])
cn <- find_connected_knn(coords_mat, k_min = 8, k_max = 30)
lw <- spdep::nb2listw(cn$nb, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)


# 4) Moran's I on residuals
moran_incRE <- spdep::moran.test(res_mu_incRE$resid, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)
# moran_noRE  <- spdep::moran.test(res_mu_noRE$resid,  lw, zero.policy = TRUE)

moran_incRE
```
